summary: Plausible latency fix for a serially-chained, one-CTA-per-token kernel (3.4-4.2 us, 3-7% of the small-M shapes), but it only works if the 8 row loads are textually issued before the first tl.sum barrier; judge on the _post_norm_combine_kernel profile row, not the sub-CI headline.
justification: Mechanism is plausible: master's _post_norm_combine_kernel (submission.py:97-118) runs one program per token with 8 static_range iterations, each 'scalar id load -> data-dependent branch -> 8 KB row load -> block-wide tl.sum (shared-memory reduction with bar.sync)'. With grid=(num_tokens,) at bs=1/8/16, at most 16 SMs are busy, so the kernel is pure latency; FINDINGS shows 3.4 us (6.6% of bs=1), 3.5 us (3.1% of bs=8), 4.2 us (3.3% of bs=16), far above the ~0.5 us that moving <=1 MB of y would cost. Predicted rows (1.6-2.5 us) are consistent with ~8 serial L2/DRAM round trips plus 8 barriered reductions collapsing to one round trip; expected directions match TASK shapes (bs<32 faster, bs>=32 untouched; shapes branch on num_tokens only). Note y was just written by the w2 Marlin so the rows are mostly L2-resident: the per-slot latency is L2 (~0.3-0.5 us incl. reduction) not DRAM, so the saving is roughly as predicted but the floor of a tiny Triton kernel in a graph (~1.3-1.8 us) caps it; bs=1 expectation of 1.6 us is optimistic, ~2 us more likely. Headline effect ~+0.5-1% geomean, below the +-1.5% CI, as the hypothesis itself admits. WEAKEST LINK: the described body still puts the load and its tl.sum in the same static_range iteration. tl.sum over a 4096-wide block lowers to a cross-warp shared-memory reduction with barriers, and LLVM/ptxas will not move global loads across bar.sync, so 'load s; reduce s; load s+1; ...' stays serial even without the branch (removing the branch only removes the id->branch dependency, not the barrier ordering). The implementer must issue all 8 masked row loads in a first phase (or, cleaner, one 2D load of a [TOP_K_C, BLOCK_H] tile with mask (ids>=0)[:,None] & mask[None,:], then ss = tl.sum(v*v, axis=1), r = rsqrt(ss/H + eps), acc = tl.sum((g_masked*r)[:,None] * v, axis=0)), and only then reduce. The per-slot scalar extraction via tl.sum(tl.where(arange==s, ids, 0)) also adds 16 small reductions; a 2D tile avoids them entirely. Numerics: the zero-row argument (g forced to 0, rsqrt(1e-8)=1e4 times 0) is correct; fp32 math and bf16 output unchanged.
confounders: post-expert-norm-triton-small-m (192f225d8f): this is the kernel being rewritten, so it is the base, not a confounder; the change is a strict in-kernel edit with the same launch site, inputs and SMALL_M_POST_NORM gate.

triton-map-align-on-block-m-restack / triton-map-align-small-m-port: _align_small_kernel produces local_ids that this kernel reads, but neither its layout nor timing changes; the align kernel precedes w13/w2 Marlin so there is no overlap interaction. Not a confounder.
marlin-block-m-two-smaller-on-postnorm and align-parallel-per-expert-verify: act only at num_tokens >= 128 / > 32, disjoint from the bs<32 shapes touched here. Not confounders.
sglang-marlin-path-parity: defines y's layout ([M, 8, H] with uninitialised remote rows), which the masked-load design respects. Not a confounder.
interference: No ab-revert is meaningful: the only overlapping landed item is the one that created this kernel, and reverting it removes the code being changed. The hypothesis bundles two sub-changes (load hoisting and num_warps 8 -> 16). A gain is attributable enough to land as a package and is read directly off the kernel row. A loss would be ambiguous between 'hoisting not realised (loads still barrier-ordered)' and '16 warps make each cross-warp reduction more expensive', but this can be diagnosed from the same run by inspecting the compiled kernel (TTGIR/PTX order of ld.global vs bar.sync, which the implementer should dump locally before checking) and does not justify spending a check on a control for a ~1% geomean item. No companions.
open_questions: Will the implementer structure the body as all-loads-then-reductions (preferably a single 2D [8, 4096] masked tile load with axis=1 sum-of-squares) rather than load+reduce per iteration? If the latter, expect little or no change.

Is num_warps=16 better than 8 for the 2D-tile form? 8 warps gives 128 fp32 live values per thread for the tile (still under the register limit) with fewer warps in each barriered reduction; worth a local microbench before checking.

Overlaps the same kernel and shapes as queued post-norm-pdl-launch-small-m; whichever lands second should be restacked on the first rather than both run against master (their gains should add: one hides launch/prologue, the other the body's latency).
If cuda-fused-moe-bs1-persistent-w13-silu-w2 or cuda-fused-moe-midm-single-launch-routed land, this kernel disappears at bs=1 or bs<=32, making this gain moot on those shapes.
